Flower Anatomy Drag & Drop Click a term in the Word Bank to highlight its location on the flower. Use Check Answer to verify.
Instructions
🎯 Objective: Identify 10 key flower parts. 🖱️ How to Play: 1. Read the term in the Word Bank (bottom). 2. Click the term button. 3. Observe the leader line and label appear on the diagram. 4. Repeat for all terms. 🔘 Action Buttons: Hint: Shows a structural clue. Check Answer: Reveals the complete key. Reset: Clears current selection. 📚 Anatomy Groups: • Perianth: Petals + Sepals • Androecium: Stamens (Filament + Anther) • Gynoecium: Pistil (Stigma, Style, Ovary) 💡 Tip: The Receptacle is the base holding all parts.

💡 Hint Panel
Petals & Sepals: Outer whorls. Petals colorful (attract pollinators), Sepals green (protect bud). Stamen (Male): Made of Filament (stalk) + Anther (pollen producer). Pistil (Female): Made of Stigma (sticky top), Style (tube), Ovary (contains ovules). Receptacle: The swollen tip of the stem holding all floral organs. Click a term in the Word Bank to see exactly where it sits on the flower.
×
✅ Answer Key & Verification
Compare your identified parts with the complete key below. In a real assessment, all 10 labels would be placed simultaneously.
1. Petal — Colorful, attracts pollinators (Corolla). 2. Sepal — Green, protects flower bud (Calyx). 3. Stamen — Male reproductive organ (Androecium). 4. Pistil — Female reproductive organ (Gynoecium). 5. Anther — Produces pollen grains (male gametes). 6. Filament — Supports the anther. 7. Ovary — Contains ovules; becomes fruit after fertilization. 8. Style — Tube connecting stigma to ovary; pollen tube grows here. 9. Stigma — Sticky surface capturing pollen. 10. Receptacle — Base attaching flower to stem (peduncle).
